title: IoT Engineer
original_description:
Do you enjoy working across the full IoT stack? In this role you’ll design embedded firmware for low-power devices, connect them through BLE, LoRa or Cellular, and build the cloud architecture and fleet management systems that run them at scale.

You’ll work closely with firmware, hardware and cloud colleagues, shape our CI/CD pipelines, and help improve how we build and deploy as we grow. It’s a hands-on role for someone who likes variety and wants to see their work running in real shipments.

📍 Location: We need you to be within commutable distance to Basel given the role requires 50%+ time spent on-site.

Founded in Switzerland in 2012, SkyCell is transforming global pharmaceutical supply chains through a combination of advanced temperature-controlled containers, IoT connectivity, and digital solutions.

Our integrated product ecosystem helps leading pharmaceutical companies reduce risk, improve operational efficiency, and ensure the safe delivery of life-saving medicines worldwide.

Today, SkyCell operates at the intersection of hardware, software, data, and logistics - combining Swiss engineering excellence with a growing digital platform to shape the future of connected pharma supply chains.

Why SkyCell?

🌱 Purpose-Driven Work: Make a real difference by contributing to a more sustainable future in global logistics and healthcare.

🚀 Innovation at Heart: Work with cutting-edge technology and be at the forefront of supply chain innovation.

🌎 Stronger together: Join a supportive team of talented individuals from over 40 countries, where we work together every step of the way.

💡 Growth Opportunities: We believe in investing in our people – continuous learning and development are key pillars of SkyCell.

🏆 Award-Winning Culture: Join a workplace recognized for its commitment to excellence with a ‘Great Place to work’ award, as well as a Platinum Ecovadis rating highlighting our sustainability and employee well-being.

What You'll Do:

  • Design and implement embedded firmware for low-power IoT devices using C/C++ (RTOS or bare-metal)

  • Integrate wireless communication technologies such as BLE, LoRa or Cellular

  • Design, build and operate cloud-side ingestion pipelines and device fleet management systems for large-scale IoT deployments

  • Contribute to the design and deployment of cloud architectures for IoT integrations

  • Implement secure and reliable OTA update mechanisms for remote firmware management

  • Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines for firmware and cloud components (e.g. GitHub Actions)

  • Collaborate with colleagues across firmware, hardware and cloud teams

  • Troubleshoot complex system-level issues across device, connectivity and cloud layers

  • Contribute to architecture and process improvements based on emerging best practices


What You'll Bring:

  • Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

  • Experience developing embedded firmware in C/C++ (RTOS or bare-metal), with a good understanding of common interfaces (I2C, SPI, UART)

  • Experience with wireless protocols (BLE, LoRa or Cellular) and IoT communication protocols and data formats (MQTT, HTTP/REST, CoAP, Protobuf, JSON)

  • Experience designing and operating cloud-based ingestion and device fleet management systems for connected IoT devices at scale

  • Experience implementing OTA updates in production systems

  • Proficiency in a backend language (e.g. Python, Go, Node.js or Java) for device integration, automation and diagnostics, with excellent system-level debugging and problem-solving skills

  • Good written and spoken German and English

If you don't meet every requirement but bring relevant experience and skills, we'd still like to hear from you.

What's In It For You?

⚡ Flexibility & Balance: Flexible working hours and work-life balance allow you to tailor work to fit your life.

🌟 Recognition & Growth: Opportunities for career advancement in a company that values your contributions.

🌍 Flexible ways of working: Our global teams work across our offices in Zurich, Zug, Hyderabad and Basel, with a mix of on-site, hybrid and remote working. Role-specific locations and working arrangements are detailed above.

🎉 Company-wide Events: Join us for company events to celebrate successes, build teams, and share our vision. Plus, new joiners experience SkyWeek, our immersive onboarding program.

👶 Generous Maternity & Paternity Leave: Support for new parents with competitive maternity and paternity leave.

🏖️ Annual Leave & Bank Holidays: Enjoy a generous annual leave package, plus local bank holidays to recharge and unwind.

Ready to Make an Impact?

We’re not just offering a job; we’re offering a chance to be part of something bigger. At SkyCell, you’ll help build a future where pharmaceutical delivery is efficient, sustainable, and transformative.

Stay Connected with SkyCell

Visit http://www.skycell.ch and explore #WeAreSkyCell on LinkedIn

How to Apply

Simply click ‘apply for this job’ below! We can’t wait to meet you and discuss how you can contribute to our mission! Please note, we are unable to consider applications sent to us via email.

If you have any questions, you can contact our Talent Team (

For this position, if you are not located in, or able to relocate (without sponsorship) to one of the advertised locations, your application cannot be considered.

title: Software Engineer - Expenses Team
original_description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

About the role

  • End-to-end expense automation: You’d work on a web app, and the BLP company card, where receipts are captured, read by AI (OCR and agents), matched to card transactions, and posted to the customer’s ERP with minimal manual effort.

  • ERP integrations and card infrastructure: We’re building interfaces to systems such as SAP, F&O, and proAlpha, along with multi-currency, fee, and tip booking logic and card transaction processing via our card partner.

  • Market expansion: We’re rolling out in Switzerland from early 2027 and in Germany from Q3 2027, which means new capabilities such as per diem allowances and kilometer expenses.

  • What’s next: Travel management integrations are planned for 2027, with automatic expense creation from bookings, handling of trip changes and cancellations, and consolidated travel reporting.

 

What you'll do

  • Drive Impact: Collaborate with business stakeholders to understand requirements and translate them into possible improvements to our product.

  • Build Great Software: Design and develop clean, maintainable, and high-quality software, applying a wide range of principles including functional patterns. Conduct code reviews and contribute to a culture of technical excellence.

  • Lead and Influence: Guide technical direction for major initiatives, shape how the product evolves and mentor team members along the way.

  • Promote Innovation and Collaboration: Work closely with colleagues, share what you learn openly, and continuously improve processes, tools, and team practices.

  • The Tech Stack for this role includes Golang, MySQL, Docker images deployed on a Kubernetes cluster in our cloud infrastructure (GCS, AWS or Azure) and Github CI/CD.

 

What you'll bring

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience.

  • 3+ years of experience in a software engineering role.

  • Passionate about software craftsmanship: Strong understanding of software development principles, Clean Code and Clean Architecture.

  • Product thinking: Ability to translate business problems into precise requirements, specifications and ultimately into code.

  • Entrepreneurial mindset: link your daily work to team and company goals, balance cost and benefit, deliver high-quality solutions efficiently.

  • Ownership: take responsibility for your technical work, for the product we build and the team we shape.

  • Team-oriented: proactively support team goals, close gaps.

  • Abstraction and efficient communication: simplify complex systems, identify core concepts, communicate complex ideas to different stakeholders.

 

What you'll get

  • Full ownership. You own the product's roadmap, from business problem to shipped code.

  • End-to-end impact. You're on a team that owns what it builds, start to finish.

  • A modern, varied tech stack. Continuous learning as the platform scales.

 

Learn more about blp and our values at blp.digital/company/careers.

title: Computational Scientist / Scientific Machine Learning
original_description:
Fusionality is building the measurement, simulation, and control stack for the fusion energy reactors of the future.

Spun out of EPFL’s Swiss Plasma Center and backed by top investors, our technology enables reliable operation, real-time monitoring, and analysis of high-temperature plasmas in fusion devices. We are founded by world-class experts at the intersection of fusion physics, advanced control, and AI (ex-Google DeepMind, EPFL). We are assembling a founding engineering team in Lausanne to build our core technology platform.

We are looking for a Computational Scientist specialized in Scientific Machine Learning (SciML) to join our team. This job is for you if you know how to write numerical solvers that are fast, correct and differentiable end to end, and want to see them run against real plasma data and inside real control systems.

We are looking for a PhD-level or senior computational researcher for this role.

Responsibilities

  • Design, implement and validate differentiable solvers in JAX for plasma physics problems such as free-boundary equilibrium, transport and state estimation.

  • Make them robust and fast enough for production use via advanced numerical techniques for differential equation time stepping, as well as optimization of GPU/TPU performance.

  • Using automatic differentiation for model calibration against experimental data, parameter estimation and controller design and optimization, working with our data and control engineers.

  • Code ownership: quality, testing, verification against reference solutions, packaging and documentation.

Requirements

  • Substantial code written in a differentiable framework. Our stack is in JAX, Julia or PyTorch experts are very welcome if they’re happy to switch.

  • Strong background in numerical methods for ODEs and PDEs: discretisation, stiff and implicit solvers, nonlinear and sparse linear solvers.

  • Demonstrated ability to operate at the frontier of SciML, Universal Differential Equations, Neural ODEs, and other emerging hybrid data-driven/mechanistic paradigms.

  • Evidence of independent work at the highest level: a PhD or thesis, published code that is used by others, or an industry project you owned.

  • Experience in the following fields an advantage but not strictly required:

  • The JAX ecosystem: Diffrax, Equinox, Optax, Lineax.

  • Plasma, fluid, electromagnetic, or other multiphysics simulation.

  • Having led the design of a scientific codebase used by others.

What we offer

  • Play a key role at a dynamic, fast-growing startup, shaping the technical solutions and products from the ground up.

  • Build cutting-edge technology to monitor and control plasmas in real fusion devices, working side-by-side with leading plasma and control experts.

  • Great working conditions, located in Lausanne, Switzerland, a city and country known for its high quality of life.

  • Competitive salary and equity compensation and benefits including immigration assistance.

original_description:
Fusionality is building the measurement, simulation, and control stack for the fusion energy reactors of the future.

Spun out of EPFL’s Swiss Plasma Center and backed by top investors, our technology enables reliable operation, real-time monitoring, and analysis of high-temperature plasmas in fusion devices. We are founded by world-class experts at the intersection of fusion physics, advanced control, and AI (ex-Google DeepMind, EPFL). We are assembling a founding engineering team in Lausanne to build our core technology platform.

We are looking for a Data / Machine Learning Engineer to join our team. This job is for you if you like turning large, messy, heterogeneous experimental data into clean, labelled, trustworthy datasets. You have done this with scientific or industrial sensor data. Familiarity with fusion is a plus but not a strict requirement.

Responsibilities

  • Build, maintain and run pipelines that bring experimental fusion data into high quality, consistent, documented, versioned datasets.

  • Develop ML-assisted labelling and event detection (e.g. disruptions, MHD activity, diagnostic faults), using weak supervision, active learning and anomaly detection.

  • Own data quality and provisioning: provenance, calibration metadata, automated validation. Manage and facilitate access for the rest of the team.

  • Work with physicists validating the datasets & labels.

  • Work with our computational scientists and control engineers, who build models and controllers on these datasets, and with customers to understand and integrate their data.

Requirements

  • Hands-on experience building data pipelines for large scientific or industrial time-series data formats (e.g. HDF5, Parquet, Zarr).

  • Proficiency in designing, querying and optimizing SQL and noSQL database systems and familiarity with Time Series databases such as TimescaleDB, InfluxDB.

  • Experience in applying ML techniques to time series in Python (PyTorch or JAX): sequence models, anomaly and event detection, semi- or weakly-supervised labelling.

  • Solid software engineering habits: testing, reproducibility, data versioning are second nature to you.

  • Evidence of independent work at the highest level: a PhD thesis and/or published code that is used by others, or an industry project you owned. You should be comfortable designing data architectures independently from day 1.

  • The following are an advantage but not strictly required:

  • Human-in-the-loop labelling tools and workflows.

  • Pipeline Orchestration (e.g. Dagster, Airflow, Prefect) and data versioning (e.g. DVC, lakeFS).

  • Data from large physics experiments: fusion, accelerators, astronomy, or exposure to fusion data systems (MDSplus, IMAS).

What we offer

  • Play a key role at a dynamic, fast-growing startup, shaping the technical solutions and products from the ground up.

  • Build cutting edge technology to monitor and control plasmas in real fusion devices, working side-by-side with leading plasma and control experts.

  • Great working conditions, located in Lausanne, Switzerland, a city and country known for its high quality of life.

  • Competitive salary and equity compensation, matched to level of seniority, and benefits including immigration assistance.

title: Senior C/C++ Low Latency Engineer
original_description:
Your job

This role is crucial for our organization. Our Technology team is small and therefore you get a lot of responsibilities and freedom! You are triggered by being faster than the competitors and you like to focus on quality. As you can imagine in a small team, there is a flat hierarchy and everybody is really hands-on to be the best in what we do!

We are looking for senior C/C++ Engineers with extensive knowledge and experience in building, testing, monitoring and maintaining large scale parallel applications and databases. As a C/C++ Engineer at Mathrix in the low latency environment, your focus will be on the code which facilitates the automated trades on various exchanges worldwide.

 

Our companies’ performance is highly dependent on the performance of our data processing pipelines. You will regularly need to appeal to all aspects of your developers’ skillset to find new and innovative ways to optimize your code. Some examples:

  • low-latency networking code for fast communication with exchanges

  • context-switch-free code

  • design and implement custom data storage structures with minimalistic footprint

  • data pipelines using a streaming paradigm

  • complex trading logic for the decision engine with the lowest possible compute time

  • re-implement existing code using advanced features of the CPU (SIMD)

 

To accommodate the growth of the company, we spend increasing efforts on the maintainability and manageability of our large, highly optimized and multithreaded codebases while preserving its main purpose (low latency). You will have to maneuver yourself between these worlds to get the best results.

 

In addition to writing code, the Technology team builds and maintains the global (hardware) infrastructure to facilitate the trading. In your job you will be regularly involved in all aspects of the pipeline and different tech stacks; from hardware compositions, network design to data logging pipelines for the traders and quants.


Who are you

Due to the growth of our organization, we are looking for more than one C/C++ Engineer. As the new team member, you bring the following skillset:

  • extensive and thorough knowledge of C and C++ in Linux

  • an understanding of – and the ability to verify - the assembly the compiler will produce from the code you write

  • understanding what (GNU/Linux) system calls you invoke will do and cost

  • knowledge of x64 hardware and how to use it efficiently

  • understanding what storage structures to select or implement given their use (time complexity)

  • ability to work with debuggers and profilers

  • operative coding (git, documentation)

  • ability to absorb from and provide knowledge to the team

  • pro-active, a self-starter, honest, flexible and stress resistant

In addition to the above, having a background in one of the specializations below are nice to have:

  • experience with network engineering; either (low latency) networking hardware deployment or networking protocol implementations

  • experience with Big Data engineering and knowledge of Big Data best practices and implementations best suited for different use cases


What we offer

  • Excellent remuneration (including discretionary bonus)

  • Fun and inspiring work environment

  • Experienced and knowledgeable colleagues

  • 25 vacation days

  • Additional benefits: going out for dinner regularly, Friday afternoon drinks, yearly office trip(s), weekly massages, monthly meal allowance

title: Lead Software Engineer
original_description:
Building the intelligence behind Solskin

Are you a driven person who wants to make buildings come alive?

We are Zurich Soft Robotics (ZSR), a Zurich-based startup developing Solskin – a climate-adaptive solar facade. Solskin is not just a PV system or a shading system; it’s an intelligent skin that uses weather and building data, occupant feedback, and AI algorithms to decide how the facade moves, so buildings stay comfortable, avoid overheating, and use energy as efficiently as possible. Solskin is already running on several buildings across Switzerland, with many more to follow.

In this role, you own the software that makes that happen. You write the code that runs Solskin, keep it reliable in the field, and constantly improve it. You will also architect and lead our future sensor-to-data platform. Your focus is where software meets hardware, and the control and AI on top of it. You don't need to be a front-end specialist.

What you will do

This is a hands-on leadership position: you code every day.

Own the full stack: You maintain and develop the whole software stack, from cloud and data management to user-facing applications, and from low-level embedded firmware to high-level AI controllers learning from users. You keep it reliable and keep making it better.

Be the link between the teams: You build the software that runs on real buildings and support the hardware team. You also build the internal tools used by sales and the business team.

Lead what comes next: With the CEO and CTO, you set the software direction and lead development of future products.

Our stack:

  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, PyTorch

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript

  • Hardware: C/C++, STM32 microcontrollers, Beckhoff PLCs

  • Database: PostgreSQL (TimescaleDB)

  • DevOps & Cloud: Linux, Docker, AWS, Grafana

What we are looking for

Required:

  • Education: MSc or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, or similar.

  • Python: This is a must. You write clean Python that runs in production, on real systems.

  • Embedded & Hardware: Shipped C/C++ on microcontrollers running on physical hardware; comfortable working with sensors, actuators, and basic electronics.

  • Applied AI & Control: Understanding of modern control and ML/RL methods, with hands-on PyTorch experience applied to physical or dynamic systems.

  • Cloud & data: You are comfortable with PostgreSQL, Docker and AWS.

  • Leadership attitude: You take ownership, make decisions, and want to grow as a leader.

  • Languages: English. German is a big plus.

  • Hybrid setting: You will be expected to be on-site at least three days per week, and sometimes at customers’ locations, to work on real products.

  • Availability: 100%, as soon as possible.

  • Work-permit: You need the right to work in Switzerland for this position.

Preferred:

  • Startup experience: You have worked in a startup before and know what that means.

  • Building modeling and control: You have prior experience handling building data, modeling building dynamics, and developing building controllers; ideally with ML and RL tools.

  • Frontend: React and TypeScript.

Mindset:

  • Hands-on: You lead, and you still do the hard work yourself.

  • Fast: You are pragmatic and iterate quickly. Things break, and plans change, and that doesn't scare you.

  • Purpose: You care about climate and want to make buildings smarter.

Benefits

Impact: Your code runs on real buildings. You see the result of your work.

Ownership: A key role with a real say in our product and technology, and room to grow with the company.

Flexibility: Hybrid work and flexible hours. We like being in the Zurich office together, so plan for regular office days.

Team: A small, skilled, and down-to-earth team that helps each other out.

The reality: We are a startup. It is often messy; things rarely work the first time, and the workload is real. In return, you get a lot of freedom and responsibility from day one.

Sounds like you?

Send us your CV and a short document instead of a classic cover letter. It doesn’t need to be long, just enough for us to understand who you are and where you stand. Please cover these points:

  • About you: A short description of yourself.

  • Proud of: One thing you are really proud of, in a few sentences.

  • Startup: Why do you fit a startup?

  • Software meets hardware: Your experience where software and hardware come together.

  • Juggeling many hats: You’ll rarely finish one thing from A to Z without interruptions: different stacks, different people, different projects, and on-site surprises. Describe a time your work was like that, and how you handled it.

title: Senior ML Engineer (Technical Lead)
original_description:
Looking for a role where you can use your ML skills to redefine how an entire industry solves core problems? We have that!
Zerolook ($1.9M raised in August 2026, founded by former Google Flights and Kayak execs) is changing how air travel is priced, and ML is at the core of our approach. As an early hire, you get to define the technical approach at the center of it all.

Tasks

  • Model Architecture: Design and implement high-performance, low-latency ML models for fare and itinerary estimation.

  • Data Engineering: Build and maintain robust data pipelines to process massive volumes of historical fare and schedule data.

  • Intelligent Routing: Develop confidence scoring systems to intelligently route traffic between ML models and current legacy stacks.

  • Domain leadership: develop core domain expertise in the field of using ML for fare and itinerary prediction.

  • Technical Leadership: hire, lead and mentor other engineers as the team grows.

  • Strategic Collaboration: Partner alongside the founders with key organizations in the industry in developing the core Zerolook offering.

Requirements

  • Education: Bachelors or Masters in Computer Science or related field.

  • Broad ML Knowledge: familiarity with the breadth of ML approaches and their relative strengths and weaknesses.

  • Production ML Expertise: 4+ years in designing, training, and deploying ML models in production environments.

  • Engineering Foundation: Strong software engineering skills with experience building robust, automated data pipelines.

  • Startup DNA: Comfortable with the "0 to 1" phase-ambiguity, fast iteration, and taking extreme ownership.

Bonus Requirements

  • Travel Tech: Previous experience with OTAs, metasearch, or GDS/NDC integration is a significant plus.

  • Large scale applications: experience building applications serving over 10K QPS at latencies on the order of 1 sec.

  • Education: Ph.D. in Computer Science and/or educational concentration in Data Science

Benefits

Compensation

CHF 140.000-150.000 + significant stock options

If you are ready to build the infrastructure that will power the next generation of travel search, we want to hear from you.

original_description:
Who is Sonar?

Sonar is driving the future of agent-centric software development. As the leader in AI code verification and governance, we solve a critical problem: ensuring that software generated by AI-assisted developers or autonomous agents is reliable, secure, and maintainable.

Integrating seamlessly with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini, and Devin, we help over 75% of the Fortune 100 build trusted, reliable, compliant software. Customers who use Sonar are 44% less likely to report an outage due to AI-generated code.

We believe code verification is the critical missing link in the Agent-Centric Development Cycle (AC/DC). Industry giants like Nvidia, ServiceNow, Booking.com, Goldman Sachs, AstraZeneca, and Ford Motor Company count on us to provide independent, explainable, consistent review and governance of their AI-generated code via products like:

  • SonarQube: The world’s leading AI code review and verification platform.
  • SonarQube Foundation Agent: Currently topping the leaderboards for agentic software repair.
  • SonarSweep & Sonar Context Augmentation: Providing the enterprise-grade context and constraints agents need to be truly effective.

Our team operates across global hubs in Austin, Bochum, Dubai, Geneva, London, Singapore, Tokyo, and Washington D.C. We move with a mindset we call CODE:

  • Committed to our customers and community.
  • Obsessed with quality.
  • Deliberate in our decisions.
  • Effective as one team.

With over $400M in revenue and profitable, fast-paced growth, we are building the backbone of the AI software revolution. If you’re hungry to have an impact, want to build at a fast pace, and ready to work at the forefront of AI, we want to hear from you.


Position description

We are looking for a driven, autonomous and impactful Staff Engineer to join the Billing Squad within our StoreFront department.

The Billing squad is one of the most cross-functional and fastest growing development teams within Sonar. We enable the release of all the new products that Sonar is currently bringing to the market, both for large and small customers. The AI-native, usage-based nature of our product offering is pushing us to rethink how we develop and implement innovative pricing models. This is pushing us to our limits every day!

You will partner closely with Product Managers, Engineering Managers, and other Staff/Principal Engineers across the organization to lead the end-to-end delivery of critical billing features. You will take ownership—from initial architecture and design through to implementation and deployment—of major initiatives ensuring a frictionless yet highly secure experience for millions of developers.


What you will do
  • Collaborate with UX designers, Product Management, and engineering teams to deliver robust security features alongside an optimal user experience.

  • Work cross functionally with product squads and go-to-market teams to ensure smooth release of new features and products.

  • Take strong ownership of squad deliverables and effectively drive sprints toward successful completion.

  • Architect and guide the design of our on-premises and AWS cloud applications.

  • Oversee feature deployment, production monitoring, and troubleshoot team-specific live issues.

  • Mentor engineering team members to help them grow in their technical responsibilities and remove blockers to their autonomy.

  • Contribute to the definition of the team’s short and long-term goals.


    • Experience and qualifications

  • Over 6 years of software engineering experience, including working as a Tech Lead, Staff Engineer, or Software Architect.

  • Proven ability to take initiative and bring a subject involving several stakeholders and engineers to completion with little to no supervision. 

  • Proficiency in working with and steering AI coding tools (Codex, Claude, etc).

  • Experience supporting and mentoring other team members.

  • Proficiency with Java coupled with a strong passion for Clean Code and rigorous software quality standards.

  • Experience architecting cloud-native applications.

  • Experience with relational RDBMS (such as Postgres) and SQL.

  • Domain expertise with billing and payment processing systems (we use Stripe)  and/or general experience with subscription management is highly desirable.

    • In-office culture

    We're intentional about this. We believe the best teams are built in the room together. Three anchor days — Mondays, Tuesdays, and Thursdays — create the collaboration rhythm that makes a hub office worth having. 

    Candidates need to be genuinely based in the location the role is posted  — if that's not where you are today, we're happy to support relocation for the right person.

     

    We value diversity, equity, and inclusion

    At Sonar, we believe that our diversity is our strength. We are a global company that values and respects different backgrounds, perspectives, and cultures. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive work environment where everyone feels valued and empowered to contribute their best. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and welcome all qualified applicants, regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

    If you need any accommodation, please reach out to us at All offers of employment at Sonar are contingent upon the results of a comprehensive background check and reference verification conducted before the start date. 

    Applications that are submitted through agencies or third party recruiters will not be considered.

title: Agentic Software Engineer (w/m/d)
original_description:
Über YOO

Sali. Wir sind YOO, die Basler Digitalagentur. Wir entwickeln digitale Lösungen, die Prozesse vereinfachen und Teams produktiver machen.

Dafür arbeiten bei uns Menschen aus unterschiedlichsten Disziplinen eng zusammen – strategisch, kreativ und technisch. Wenn du Verantwortung übernehmen und im digitalen Projektalltag etwas bewegen willst, bist du bei uns richtig. Wir suchen per sofort oder nach Vereinbarung.

Aufgaben

  • Entwicklung von Softwarelösungen für Kund:innen aus unterschiedlichsten Branchen.

  • Effektiver Einsatz von Coding Agents, LLMs und AI APIs im Entwicklungsalltag.

  • Anforderungen von Kund:innen verstehen und gemeinsam mit UX, Design und Projektmanagement kritisch auf Vollständigkeit, Eindeutigkeit und technische Machbarkeit prüfen.

  • Features so spezifizieren, dass sie effizient AI-gestützt umgesetzt werden können.

  • Aktive Mitgestaltung unserer AI-gestützten Entwicklungsprozesse (Tooling, Workflows, Guidelines), um Kundenlösungen schneller und besser umzusetzen.

Qualifikation

  • Mindestens fünf Jahre Erfahrung in der professionellen Softwareentwicklung.

  • Fundierte Kenntnisse in Software-Architektur und Software-Design.

  • Praktische Erfahrung im Einsatz von AI Coding Tools (z. B. Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor) sowie ein gutes Verständnis der Möglichkeiten und Grenzen von LLMs und agentic Softwareentwicklung.

  • Erfahrung mit Git-Workflows, CI/CD und automatisiertem Testing, damit AI-generierter Code in Kundenprojekten zuverlässig abgesichert ist.

  • Eine strukturierte, eigenverantwortliche Arbeitsweise und Freude an neuen Technologien.

  • Erfahrung mit Microsoft Azure und cloudbasierten Architekturen sowie mit Docker oder Kubernetes ist ein Plus.

  • Du bringst sehr gute Deutsch- (C2) und gute Englischkenntnisse (B2) mit.

Benefits

  • Work-Life Integration mit flexiblen Arbeitszeiten, Homeoffice und Workation.

  • Ein sympathisches Team, das sich auf dich freut und dir hilft, schnell Fuss zu fassen sowie aktive Mitgestaltungsmöglichkeiten und flache Hierarchien.

  • Förderung bei Weiterbildungen und Beteiligung am Unternehmensgewinn.

  • Modernes Büro in Gehdistanz zum Bahnhof SBB.

  • Unfallzusatzversicherung und attraktiver BVG-Leistungsplan.

  • Lebendige Teamkultur mit Spiel, Sport und Spass.

title: Senior Control Systems Engineer
original_description:
Fusionality is building the measurement, simulation and control stack of the fusion energy reactors of the future.

Our technology enables effective and reliable operation, monitoring, and analysis of high-temperature plasmas in fusion devices — which will one day provide clean, practically limitless power to the grid. We have spun out of EPFL’s Swiss Plasma Center and have just completed our pre-seed fundraise.

We are looking for a Senior Control Systems Engineer to join our founding team in Lausanne and help build our core technology.

This job is for you if you are a passionate engineer with deep knowledge cutting across real-time / embedded systems, software and hardware, and excited about building the systems to monitor and control real-world fusion plasmas.

Tasks

  • Implement real-time control, analysis, data acquisition systems in the kHz to MHz range, as individual contributor and in a team.
  • Integrate solutions across a variety of company products and services as well as on our in-house test beds.
  • Provide technical leadership within a growing real-time control and software engineering team that you will help to build.
  • Translate customer needs into requirements and specifications.

Requirements

  • Experience taking hard-real-time acquisition and control loops from incomplete requirements through to commissioning on hardware, in domains such as automotive, robotics, embedded, electrical and/or scientific instrumentation.
  • ‘Full stack’: familiarity with all aspects of real-time technologies, from physical/DAQ, real-time software frameworks and middleware, real-time OS and integration.
  • Fluency in a mix of high-level and low-level languages such as C, C++, Rust, MATLAB/Simulink, Python. Obsession with code quality, testing and reliability.
  • Experience with distributed real-time systems, real-time networking and field buses and/or SCADA is an advantage.
  • Experience with embedded/μC/FPGA technologies and/or safety critical systems is an advantage.

Benefits

  • The unique opportunity to play a foundational role at a dynamic, fast-growing startup, shaping the technical solutions and products from the ground up.
  • The opportunity to build cutting edge technology to monitor and control plasmas in real fusion devices, working side-by-side with leading plasma and control experts.
  • Great working conditions, located in Lausanne, Switzerland, a city and country known for its high quality of life.
  • Competitive salary and equity compensation and benefits including immigration assistance.

If you are excited about joining our team, send your CV including information about a real-time system you have taken into operation. We're looking forward to hearing from you.

title: (Senior) Integration Engineer, ERP (Oracle)
original_description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

About the role

BLP only works when it talks to our customers’ ERP systems. As an Integration Engineer, you build and own those connections and keep live integrations running for enterprise customers. Every new ERP system is a new problem to solve. You’ll lead our Oracle integrations across Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite and JD Edwards, while also contributing to other integrations.

 

What you’ll do

  • Own our integrations with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite and JD Edwards and ensure their market fit, usability and reliability.

  • Design and implement interfaces for diverse protocols: REST, SOAP, direct DB access and file transfers.

  • Explore new ERP systems and determine the best way to connect them.

  • Build new ERP integrations, often in close collaboration with pilot customers.

  • Own existing integrations end to end, including issue resolution, and document them so teammates can pick them up.

  • Enable technical project managers to consult on, install and configure mature integrations.

 

What you'll bring

  • Hands-on integration experience with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards EnterpriseOne, ideally more than one. You have built or maintained interfaces yourself, not only used the system as a functional consultant or key user.

  • Experience with the native interfaces of at least one of these:

    • Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP: REST and SOAP web services, File-Based Data Import (FBDI) through the ERP Integration Service, and data extraction with BI Publisher or BI Cloud Connector (BICC).

    • NetSuite: SuiteTalk REST and SOAP web services, SuiteQL, SuiteScript 2.x (e.g., RESTlets, Map/Reduce scripts), and Token-Based Authentication or OAuth 2.0.

    • JD Edwards EnterpriseOne: AIS Server and Orchestrator, Business Services (BSSV), and Z-file interface tables (e.g., F0411Z1) with their batch processors.

  • A good understanding of purchase-to-pay data in Oracle ERPs: suppliers, purchase orders, receipts and supplier invoice matching.

  • Solid programming skills in at least one backend language. We build our integrations in Go. If you come from Java, C#, Python or similar and are keen to pick up Go, that works for us.

  • A degree in computer science or a related field, or equivalent experience.

  • A structured, self-reliant way of working, and ideally experience in a client-facing role.

  • Fluent English. German is a plus, as most of our customers are in the DACH region.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with both cloud (Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite) and on-premise (JD Edwards) environments, and the constraints of each (e.g., no direct database access in Fusion, governance limits in NetSuite).

  • Extensive experience with SQL, common data formats (JSON, XML, CSV) and transports (REST/SOAP APIs, SFTP).

  • Familiarity with modern engineering practices: Git, code reviews, automated testing and CI/CD.

  • Integration experience with other ERPs, such as SAP, Microsoft Dynamics or Infor.

 

Integration Engineer or Senior Integration Engineer

We hire at both levels. Four things decide where you start: years of experience, breadth of experience, coaching experience and scope.

Integration Engineer

  • Years: 2+ years of hands-on integration work, including Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards.

  • Breadth: in-depth experience with one Oracle ERP and its interfaces.

  • Coaching: you learn quickly from senior colleagues and share what you learn with the team.

  • Scope: you deliver and maintain integrations and resolve issues independently, with guidance on architecture decisions.

Senior Integration Engineer

  • Years: 5+ years of hands-on integration work, several of them with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards.

  • Breadth: integration experience across two or more of Fusion, NetSuite and JD Edwards, or across Oracle and other ERPs, in cloud and on-premise environments.

  • Coaching: you have coached or mentored other engineers and help technical project managers grow.

  • Scope: you own our Oracle integrations end to end, set technical direction and take on the most complex customer cases.

Why BLP

  • Real impact: your integrations decide whether a customer goes live.

  • Breadth: Oracle, Infor, Microsoft Dynamics and many other ERPs, plus EDI and e-invoicing standards.

  • Growth: fast-tracked growth, with promotions and a bonus scheme that includes company shares.

  • Team: regular team events.

Practical information

  • Location: our Zurich office, hybrid with 3+ office days per week, or remotely from anywhere in Europe.

  • If you work remotely, we pay for regular visits and stays in Zurich.

  • Employment: full-time, permanent.

 

Learn more about blp and our values at blp.digital/company/careers.

title: Site Reliability Engineer
original_description:
About Us:

DeepJudge is Switzerland’s leading AI and ICT scale-up, transforming how law firms and legal departments access and leverage their knowledge. Founded by former Google search engineers with PhDs in AI from ETH Zurich, and backed by top-tier Silicon Valley investors, we are building the intelligence layer that powers the legal industry.

Every firm can license the same AI models, but no two firms share the same institutional knowledge. Decades of experience, work product, and precedent are often trapped across systems, underused and inaccessible. title: Synthesis Instrumentation Engineer
original_description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

We're looking for a hands-on scientist-engineer to help build our next-generation DNA synthesis platform, enabling high-throughput, cost-effective production of large and diverse DNA libraries. You'll work at the intersection of chemistry, materials science, bioengineering, and hardware development, designing and building prototypes, running experiments, and optimizing processes to turn new synthesis technologies into reliable, scalable production systems.

DNA synthesis is a fundamental part of our protein engineering platform. We're developing new approaches to dramatically increase synthesis throughput while reducing cost and turnaround time.

You'll work closely with our scientific and engineering teams to develop and prototype new DNA synthesis technologies. Your focus will be on translating scientific concepts into working hardware and experimental systems, designing and building prototypes, testing different approaches, and continuously improving their performance.

This is a highly hands-on, interdisciplinary role combining experimental science with practical engineering. You'll take ownership of prototype development, experimental validation, and process optimization, helping move promising technologies from early concepts to reliable, scalable systems.

We're looking for someone who enjoys building things, solving technical problems, and working across disciplines. You don't need to be an expert in DNA synthesis, but you should have strong scientific fundamentals, an engineering mindset, and experience turning ideas into working prototypes.

What You'll Do

  • Design, build, and test prototypes for next-generation DNA synthesis technologies.

  • Translate scientific and technical requirements into practical engineering designs and experimental setups.

  • Scope and evaluate different technical approaches, components, materials, and equipment for prototype development.

  • Develop and optimize the chemistry, materials, and processes underlying the synthesis platform.

  • Design and execute experiments to characterize performance, identify limitations, and improve reliability.

  • Work closely with mechanical, electronics, software, and automation engineers to develop integrated experimental systems.

  • Troubleshoot complex technical problems across chemistry, hardware, and process engineering.

  • Develop analytical methods and quality control strategies to measure performance and guide optimization.

  • Help scale successful prototypes into robust, reproducible systems suitable for routine production.

  • Work with external suppliers and engineering partners to source components, evaluate technologies, and accelerate development.

What We're Looking For

  • A strong background in chemical engineering, chemistry, materials science, bioengineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field.

  • Hands-on experience designing, building, and testing experimental setups, prototypes, or laboratory equipment.

  • Strong understanding of chemistry, materials, or process engineering, with the ability to apply these fundamentals to practical engineering challenges.

  • Experience developing and optimizing experimental processes, including systematic troubleshooting and performance characterization.

  • Comfortable working across hardware and experimental science, translating scientific requirements into practical engineering solutions.

  • Experience selecting components, evaluating technical trade-offs, and iterating on prototype designs.

  • Strong experimental skills, including designing experiments, analyzing data, and making decisions based on results.

  • Independent, resourceful, and comfortable working on open-ended technical problems.

  • A practical, hands-on approach to engineering, with a focus on building, testing, and improving systems rather than purely theoretical development.

  • Experience with DNA or oligonucleotide synthesis, including chemical or enzymatic approaches, is a plus.

  • Experience with solid-phase synthesis, surface chemistry, or chemical process development is a plus.

  • Familiarity with microfluidics, high-throughput dispensing, or array-based technologies is a plus.

  • Experience with laboratory automation, instrumentation, or custom hardware development is a plus.

  • Experience with CAD, electronics, fluidics, or mechanical prototyping is a plus.

  • Experience scaling experimental technologies from proof of concept to production is a plus.

  • Programming and data analysis experience, particularly in Python, is a plus.

Details

  • Location: Lausanne, Switzerland (on-site)

  • Type: Full time

  • Start date: ASAP

Application deadline

We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

You'll work across LabOS — our internal software platform — building the orchestration layer that coordinates everything from experiment scheduling to execution to data capture and results processing. Day-to-day, that can mean things like:

  • Building custom AI agents and tooling that automate decisions across the experiment lifecycle, from protocol design to troubleshooting failed results

  • Turning proprietary hardware into API-controllable devices that agents and software can operate programmatically

  • Designing scheduling systems that coordinate dozens of lab instruments with complex dependency chains

You'll own large areas of the product. We're a small team where individual engineers have large impact on what gets built and how.

What we're looking for

  • Full-stack production experience. We use TypeScript, React, Node, Postgres — but what matters is you can work across the stack.

  • Product instinct. You've shipped, watched users, iterated, and shipped again.

  • Comfortable in ambiguity. You start from a goal, not a spec. You scope problems down, decide what to build and what to skip, and write your own plan when none exists.

  • Builds with AI. You use AI tools heavily, but you have enough experience without them to know what good looks like.

  • Curious about biology. No background required, but running real experiments in the physical world should excite you.

We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

original_description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

We're building highly automated laboratory systems that combine robotics, scientific instruments, custom hardware, and software to run biological experiments at scale.

You'll help design, prototype, and build the mechanical and mechatronic systems that connect and support our laboratory automation infrastructure. This includes developing custom components, integrating sensors and actuators, improving existing systems, and solving practical engineering challenges that arise as we scale.

This is a highly hands-on role. You'll work alongside our automation engineers on projects from initial concept and CAD through prototyping, testing and deployment in the lab, and take on more ownership as you grow. You'll work closely with our automation, software, and biology teams to develop reliable hardware that can operate continuously with minimal human intervention.

We're looking for someone who enjoys building things, learning quickly and solving practical technical problems, and turning ideas into working systems. If you've spent your studies building robots, rockets, race cars or 3D-printed contraptions and want to do that full-time on real problems, we'd love to hear from you.

Location: Lausanne, Switzerland (on-site) · Type: Full-time · Experience: 0–3 years (recent graduates welcome)

What You'll Do

  • Design, prototype, and build custom mechanical and mechatronic components for laboratory automation.

  • Develop fixtures, mounts, enclosures, robotic interfaces, and other custom hardware.

  • Integrate sensors, actuators, motors, and control electronics with guidance from senior engineers, improving automation capabilities and system monitoring.

  • Take designs from CAD through fabrication, assembly, testing and deployment.

  • Help integrate new hardware and scientific instruments into automated workflows.

  • Troubleshoot mechanical, electrical and integration issues, learning to find root causes and build robust fixes.

  • Contribute to improving existing hardware for reliability and maintainability.

  • Help source components and work with suppliers on custom parts.

What We're Looking For

  • A degree (BSc or MSc) in mechanical engineering, mechatronics, robotics or a related field.

  • Hands-on experience designing and building physical things, whether from internships, a thesis, student teams (e.g. Formula Student, EPFL Xplore/Rocket Team, robotics competitions) or personal projects.

  • Comfortable with CAD (SolidWorks, Fusion 360, Onshape or similar).

  • Experience with 3D printing, basic machining or mechanical assembly.

  • Comfortable working safely in a workshop with hand and power tools (e.g. drills, saws, grinders).

  • Some exposure to sensors, motors or basic electronics (Arduino-level is great).

  • Curious, eager to learn, and happy to get your hands dirty. You ask good questions and take initiative.

Nice to Have

None of these are required. They're things you'll pick up here.

  • Exposure to laboratory automation, scientific instrumentation, or robotic systems.

  • Experience with data acquisition or sensor integration.

  • Familiarity with PCB design, embedded electronics, microcontrollers, or control systems.

  • Experience with fluidics, pneumatics, or vacuum systems.

  • Experience operating workshop machinery such as a lathe, milling machine, CNC or laser cutter.

  • Programming experience in Python, C/C++, or similar languages.

  • A solid grounding in mechanical design principles, materials and tolerances.

  • Membership of a student competition team, or open-source hardware or maker projects.

Application deadline

We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

Language: Fluency in a two European languages in addition to English.

About Us

Point One Navigation is building the future of precise location. Our mission is to deliver a unified location platform that enables autonomy, safety, and efficiency across industries from robotics to transportation. We are a high-performance, high-collaboration team that thrives on solving complex problems, moving fast, and delivering impact.

Role Outcome

The Network Customer Support Engineer owns the customer support experience tied to the reliability, visibility, and operational health of Point One’s correction network.

Success in this role means:

  • Potential customer facing issues are identified and addressed before they impact customers.

  • When incidents do occur, they are resolved quickly with clear communication and strong root-cause analysis.

  • The organization has clear visibility into network health, operational trends, and customer friction.

  • A scalable network operations and support function is built as the company and network footprint grow.

Immediate Areas of Focus

Own the customer experience of our Network

  • Work with our Network Operations team to understand incidents that affect the customer experience

  • Identify emerging issues and collaborate with engineering and manufacturing teams to understand and support the resolution of those issues.

  • Understand available metrics and dashboards and contribute to the development of these tools to allow for the targeted resolution of customer questions.

Deliver High-Quality Technical Support

  • Liaison between Engineering, Network Operations and FAE and FDE team to support the customer.

  • Personally manage high-impact or technically complex support cases.

  • Partner closely with FAEs, Product, and Engineering to diagnose issues and close the loop with customers.

  • Ensure customers receive clear, confident communication during investigations and incidents.

  • Model best-in-class technical troubleshooting and customer engagement practices for the team.

Build the Foundation for a Scalable Operations & Support Function

  • Design and implement systems that enable both network operations and customer support to scale.

  • Define a support ticket taxonomy that reflects customer use cases, technical complexity, and operational impact.

  • Support Network Ops team on operational metrics such as:

    • Network uptime and availability

    • Incident response and resolution times

    • Support response and resolution times

    • Alert quality and monitoring coverage

    • Document operational procedures, escalation paths, and ownership models.

  • Develop automation and tooling to reduce manual work and improve operational efficiency.

Surface Operational and Customer Insights

  • Identify patterns across support tickets, network events, and operational data.

  • Translate operational signals into actionable insights for Product and Engineering.

  • Ensure recurring issues and infrastructure gaps are clearly surfaced and prioritized.

Establish Visibility Into Customer Experience

  • Define and implement the right metrics for understanding customer experience and operational impact.

  • Establish mechanisms to collect structured customer feedback without creating noise.

  • Use both operational data and customer feedback to drive continuous improvement.

Coach and Develop the Operations & Support Function

  • Act as a player-coach, leading through hands-on operational work while building the foundations of the team.

  • Train and mentor support engineers on troubleshooting methodology, operational awareness, and customer communication.

  • Continuously raise the operational and support bar as the team grows.

Qualifications

  • Fluency in a two European languages in addition to English.

  • Experience in a player-coach technical operations or support role where you owned both hands-on troubleshooting and operational systems.

  • Bias toward ownership, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.

Our Cultural Foundation

At Point One, our cultural and operating design is built around one guiding principle: we must move with extreme speed and efficiency of effort to stay in a leadership position.

This environment gives people a high level of autonomy and the ability to make a real impact. It also challenges every team member to grow — both professionally and personally. Because we focus on promoting from within rather than relying on external hiring, the opportunities for advancement are tremendous for those who seek them.

That said, growth only comes from delivering in the present. What matters most is the job to be done today, not the job you want tomorrow. When we all focus on today’s outcomes with excellence, the path to greater responsibility and growth naturally follows.

We think about our culture in two dimensions:

How We Show Up Every Day

These are the behaviors we expect every team member to bring to work — the foundation of being a consummate, high-output teammate:

  • Trust / Assume Best Intent — Trust allows us to move fast. When we start from trust, we spend no time second-guessing or looking for ulterior motives and thus focus all our energy on acting.

  • High Output, Action Oriented — Our default posture is “yes.” We bias toward action and deliver results quickly, knowing that speed and efficiency compound into impact as we unblock others around us.

  • No Ego, One Team — Collaboration without ego creates leverage. When we win as one team, we eliminate friction and move faster together.

  • Self Accountability — Taking ownership is the straightest line to learning, self-improvement, and correcting our course of action. And blaming others around us is a fast path to destroying trust.

Operating Principles

These are the systems and norms that amplify speed and efficiency at the company level:

  • Edge Innovation — We bias toward action over approval. Experiment, decide, and move — failure is just a step toward faster learning.

  • No Hierarchies — We practice self-prioritization and go direct to the source. Flattening layers reduces drag and maximizes autonomy.

  • Customer Experience First — We optimize for the end-to-end customer outcome, not functional or departmental efficiency. This focus cuts waste, aligns priorities, and ensures we spend effort where it matters most.

title: Head of Software Engineering
original_description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

You'll be a player-coach — someone who still ships code but also owns the engineering roadmap, team structure, and technical direction. You'll translate company strategy into engineering priorities, make sure the right things get built in the right order, and help a small, high-output team scale without losing speed.

You'll lead a small, technical engineering team that leverages AI to build the software infrastructure for running our automated lab. Your job is to make it the best small engineering team in biotech, and grow it thoughtfully as we scale.

This is not a management-track role where you stop building. You'll stay hands-on, especially as AI agents reshape what a small engineering team can accomplish. We expect you to be deeply technical, opinionated about architecture, and actively shipping — while also being the person who ensures the whole engineering org is pointed in the right direction and moving fast.

Day-to-day, that can mean:

  • Owning the engineering roadmap — deciding what to build, what to defer, and what to kill

  • Setting technical direction and architecture across frontend, backend, data pipelines, and lab-hardware integration

  • Shipping code yourself on the highest-leverage problems, not just reviewing it

  • Hiring, growing, and setting the bar for a team that ships fast and holds quality high — our lab runs on this software, so when things break, real experiments fail and real customers are affected

  • Building the team's AI-assisted development practices into a genuine speed advantage

What we're looking for

  • Still building. You've shipped production software for years and you're not looking to leave the code behind — you want a role where you build and lead at the same time.

  • You've built teams. You've hired, managed, and developed engineers, and built a team that ships fast and holds a high bar — at least once before, in a startup or high-growth environment.

  • Roadmap ownership. You've owned or significantly shaped an engineering roadmap. You've made the call on what to build, defer, and kill — and you make pragmatic tradeoffs that keep things shipping and stop projects from growing out of scope.

  • Technical breadth. You make good architectural decisions across frontend, backend, data, and infrastructure, and you know when to go deep versus when to delegate.

  • AI-native. It's 2026 — you already build with AI agents and coding tools as a force multiplier, and you have a real point of view on how they change team structure, tooling, and workflow.

  • A genuine interest in biology. No background required, but our product is running biology experiments in the physical world and that should excite you.

  • High-autonomy, founder mindset. We share context and vision openly. You figure out what matters most and go work on it.

Application deadline

We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

title: Lab Automation Engineer
original_description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

We build our lab automation ourselves. Instead of buying turnkey systems and running them through a vendor's GUI, we reverse-engineer instruments, control them with open-source Python tooling like PyLabRobot and PyHamilton, and build the software and hardware to turn a pile of instruments into work cells that run biology around the clock.

We're looking for a Lab Automation Engineer to help design, build, and run these systems. This is a broad role: on any given week you might be writing a driver for a new instrument, getting a liquid handler and a robot arm to hand off cleanly, or debugging why an overnight run stalled. We care far more about range, ability, and drive than years on any one platform.

 

What You'll Do

  • Control lab instruments — liquid handlers, robot arms, plate readers, incubators, analytical devices — programmatically in Python, ideally with PyLabRobot / PyHamilton, rather than locking workflows into proprietary software.

  • Build and integrate work cells: get multiple instruments working together as one orchestrated unit that runs unattended.

  • Bring new instruments online by reverse-engineering their control protocols and building drivers that expose them to the rest of the stack.

  • Write the software glue — drivers, integrations, small services — that connects hardware to our platform (mostly Python, with some TypeScript).

  • Partner with biologists to turn new assays into reliable automated workflows, then keep them running: diagnosing and fixing the mechanical, electrical, and software failures that come with 24/7 production.

  • Push throughput and reliability up continuously — better error recovery, smarter scheduling, sturdier hardware.

 

What We're Looking For

  • Maker and hacker attitude. You like taking systems apart, figuring out how they work, and building the thing that makes them work better. You'd rather script an instrument than click through it.

  • Strong software engineering skills. You write real Python and can structure code others can maintain — drivers, integrations, services — not just throwaway scripts. You'll pick up TypeScript where needed.

  • Lab automation experience. Hands-on with PyHamilton, PyLabRobot, Opentrons, or similar tooling is a strong plus. Direct experience automating instruments and workflows matters more than the specific platform.

  • Self-starter and independent. You see what needs building and build it. You don't wait for a spec, and you don't need a vendor training course to get going.

  • AI-native builder. It's 2026 — you build with coding agents like Claude Code as a default, and you have sharp judgment about what they produce.

  • Hardware comfort is a plus. Electronics, microcontrollers, 3D printing, CAD, or fabrication experience all help, but they're not required if your software and automation skills are strong.

  • Debugging instinct. When something fails mid-run, you reason across software, firmware, electronics, and mechanics to find the cause and fix it.

Biology background not required — but you should be excited that the robots run real experiments.

 

Details

  • Location: Lausanne, Switzerland (on-site — you're building physical systems)

  • Type: Full time

  • Start date: ASAP

Application deadline

We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

original_description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

You'll build work-cell orchestration, instrument drivers, protocol scheduling, error-recovery logic, and monitoring. Physical systems fail in ways pure software doesn't — a plate gets stuck, a liquid handler skips a well, a temperature controller drifts. Your job is to make the system handle all of it gracefully. This is a broad, hands-on role for a strong engineer who wants their code to drive real machines and see it run the same day.

What You'll Do

  • Build orchestration software that coordinates liquid handlers, plate readers, incubators, and robot arms — handling timing dependencies, state, and error recovery.

  • Reverse-engineer and develop instrument drivers and APIs. Each instrument speaks a different protocol (serial, USB, TCP/IP); you work out how it talks and build a clean abstraction over it.

  • Model and execute complex multi-step protocols reliably — a single run can span dozens of steps across multiple instruments.

  • Build error-recovery logic so that when something fails mid-run, the system retries, skips, alerts, or pauses depending on the failure mode.

  • Create monitoring and observability for work-cell health: instrument status, run progress, error rates.

  • Debug across the software–hardware boundary — figuring out whether bad data is a comms, firmware, calibration, or code problem.

  • Work closely with lab automation engineers, the rest of the software team, and the scientists running production.

Stack

TypeScript and Python, Postgres (Supabase), Modal for compute. We control instruments with open-source Python tooling like PyLabRobot and PyHamilton wherever we can, rather than proprietary vendor GUIs.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering skills. You write production code in Python and/or TypeScript — well-structured and maintainable, not just prototypes.

  • Comfortable at the hardware-software boundary. You've built software that drives physical devices, or you're excited to. You can read a protocol spec, debug a flaky connection, and reason about timing.

  • Lab automation experience is a strong plus. Familiarity with PyHamilton, PyLabRobot, Opentrons, or similar tooling helps — as does a background in robotics, industrial automation, IoT, or embedded systems.

  • Maker and hacker attitude. You like figuring out how closed systems work and building the thing that makes them work better. Bonus if you're comfortable with electronics, microcontrollers, or a 3D printer when an integration needs a physical fix.

  • AI-native builder. It's 2026 — you build with coding agents like Claude Code as a default, and you have sharp judgment about what they produce.

  • Self-starter and independent. You define what needs building from how the lab actually works, not just what's in the ticket.

  • Reliability-minded. The lab runs 24/7; you design systems where one instrument failing doesn't cascade through the whole work cell.

Biology background not required — but you should be excited that the code runs real experiments.

Details

  • Location: Lausanne, Switzerland (on-site — you need hands-on access to physical instruments).

  • Type: Full time

  • Start date: ASAP

title: R&D Mechanical Engineer
original_description:
As a R&D Mechanical Engineer within our Mechanical team, you will lead development of mechanical systems and subsystems of our next-generation surgical robot from the early concept to the to a verified product.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

R&D & Mechatronic Subsystem Design

• Lead the end-to-end design and development of high-precision mechatronic subsystems for surgical robotics, translating clinical and industrial design inputs into simple and robust mechanical solutions.

• Execute detailed design work utilizing 3D CAD (Solidworks), finite element analysis (FEA), and worst-case tolerance stack-up analyses. And applying DFM/DFA principles to optimize cost, yield, and assembly efficiency.

• Collaborate within cross-functional R&D teams (Electrical, Software, Systems, and Clinical) to rapidly prototype, validate, and iterate robotic platforms and subsystems.

Verification, Testing & Tooling

• Architect, build and document custom mechatronic test benches and automated test fixtures for design verification, fatigue testing, and end-of-line production testing.

• Author and execute verification protocols and reports to prove subsystem performance against medical device requirements.

Design Transfer & Supply Chain

• Support Design Transfer to Contract Manufacturers, by transferring technical knowledge to industrialization teams, reviewing Work Instructions and pFMEAs, and supporting process-specific tool development.

• Support mechanical supplier selection and qualification, support root-cause analyses for supplier-related quality issues (NC/CAPA).

Medical Device Compliance & Lifecycle

• Maintain full compliance with medical device standards (e.g., ISO 13485, IEC 60601-1, ISO 14971) and author compliant Design History File (DHF) documentation.

• Plan and execute Engineering Change Requests, ensuring robust risk management and traceability.

• Chair formal technical design reviews and present architectural decisions to cross-departmental stakeholders and leadership.

Requirements

Work Experience and Education requirements:

• Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics or a related engineering discipline.

• Relevant Experience: Minimum of 3+ years of professional mechanical design experience, with ideally direct expertise in collaborative robots (cobots), robotics platforms, or high-precision robotic joints/actuators.

• Full-Lifecycle DFX Mastery: Proven track record in end-to-end product design, incorporating Design for Excellence principles:

o Design for Manufacturability & Assembly (DFM/DFA)

o Design to Cost (DTC)

o Design for Reliability & Serviceability (DFR/DFS)

• Testing & Prototyping: Demonstrated hands-on experience with rapid prototyping, physical assembly, formal design reviews, and reliability/verification testing.

• Language Skills: Professional proficiency in written and spoken English, with strong technical communication skills

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities required:

• SolidWorks & Multi-Process Manufacturing: Expert-level proficiency in 3D CAD (SolidWorks) with deep domain knowledge in designing components for diverse manufacturing processes, including:

o CNC Machining & Precision Milling

o Metal Casting, Forging & Sheet Metal Fabrication

o Additive Manufacturing / 3D Printing

o Injection Molding

• Cross-Functional & Supplier Management: Strong ability to lead technical execution with external development partners, contract manufacturers, and component vendors, as well as collaborating across interdisciplinary R&D teams (Software, Electrical, Systems, Quality).

• Analytical Problem Solving: Passion for dissecting complex mechanical challenges and engineering elegant, simple, high-reliability solutions for robotics.

• Drive & Ownership: Self-motivated engineer with high autonomy who thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative team environment, maintaining accountability, technical curiosity, and a positive team culture

Benefits

What we offer:

  • A dynamic, innovative environment with cutting-edge medical technology that is shaping the future of robotic surgery.
  • Fast-growing Company where innovation meets agility.
  • Structured onboarding program and training, ensuring a confident start.
  • High degree of autonomy and flexibility.
